findings.title: Deposit is within the amount cap
findings.detail: This amount check does not verify deposit protection or authenticity. Annual rent GBP 15600; cap = 15600 / 52 * 5 (GBP 1500.00 rounded down to pennies); requested GBP 1500. Importance: 85/100. Conditional: Confirm that the rented property is in England. Confirm this is an ordinary private tenancy, not an excluded arrangement. Confirm that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The cap calculation is correct on the supplied figures: GBP 1300 x 12 = GBP 15,600 a year; 15,600 / 52 x 5 = GBP 1,500.00; the stated deposit is GBP 1,500, so the amount is at the cap and not above it. This is a limited amount-cap pass. It does not show the deposit is protected or the arrangement is authentic. The cap's applicability is still unresolved: the jurisdiction and tenancy type are unknown, and the contract does not confirm that the rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy or that the arrangement is not excluded. I cannot dismiss the issue or overturn the calculation. It stays conditional on those facts. Sources: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/tenant-fees-act-2019-guidance-for-tenants

findings.title: Managing agent appointment attachment not supplied
findings.detail: The contract refers to a separate attachment about the owner's appointment of the managing agent, but its content is not in the supplied material. It is not found in the evidence bundle; this does not show it does not exist or that anything is unlawful. The document should be requested. Importance: 45/100. Conditional: Content of the attachment is unknown, so its relevance to fees or obligations cannot be assessed. The referenced material was not found in the supplied contract. Paragraph 11 refers to a separate attachment about the owner's appointment of the managing agent, and the bundle says it is not included. No other segment supplies that material. Its absence does not show that the attachment does not exist or that anything is unlawful. Its contents are needed before its relevance to fees, authority or obligations can be assessed, so the issue stays conditional until the attachment is supplied.
